guidelines.detail: same as LRN-005 (The description opens with an employee or department submitting a request. The reference models this as a start event followed by a submission task (F22, M2). The generated model instead uses a start event named 'Request submitted', which is the resulting state, and sends it straight to the assessment task (X1, G1). The submission action is therefore lost. The records support the existing learned )

same as LRN-019 (The generated model merged a compatibility check with cost and resource assessment into one task (P2), so the reference task for the compatibility check has no counterpart (M1), which is a label-level semantic divergence. The records show a real difference, so I propose the guideline. It is essentially the same as the learned guideline LRN-019 and the previously recorded guideline, so it is classe)

same as LRN-008 (The generated model has no parallel split after the submitted request and no parallel join before the approval decision, so the two assessment activities are not synchronized. LRN-008 already requires a parallel split and join for side-by-side activities that a later step needs, and LRN-016 says the same for independent activities. The new element here is that the join must come before a decision )

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description opens by saying that the process starts when a participant performs a named action (for example identifying a need), so that action is a performed step that precedes the first described activity: Model a plain start event with no label that carries the action. Add a task named for the participant's action, placed after the start event and before the first described activity. Route the sequence flow start event, then action task, then the first activity. Do not put the action into the start event's label, and do not drop the action because the trigger already implies it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process starts when a participant performs a named submission action (for example, submitting a request), and that action is a performed step rather than a message or condition

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description lists several distinct evaluations of the same artifact in one sentence, separated by commas or 'and': Model each listed evaluation as its own task, in the order the description states them, and connect the tasks in sequence. Do not combine them into one task whose label lists all the evaluations. Place any outcome that the description attaches to the evaluations after the last task of the sequence.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states one step whose sentence lists several separately named checks or assessments of the same request or artifact (for example, checking compatibility and also assessing cost and resource needs), joined by commas or 'and', so the listed checks are distinct actions

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names several activities that are carried out side by side, with no stated order among them, and a later step starts only after all of them are finished: Model a parallel split gateway before the group of activities, with one unconditional outgoing flow to each activity. Join the activities with a parallel join gateway, and connect one outgoing flow from that join to the later step. Do not add decision conditions to these branches, and do not chain the activities in sequence when the description does not order them.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that two or more activities are carried out together after one step, with no stated order among them, and the next step is a decision that depends on the results of all of them
